name: Fluoxetine Hydrochloride
sections: White crystalline solid (hydrochloride); melting point 179–182 °C; racemic mixture.
Developed by Bryan Molloy, David Wong and colleagues at Eli Lilly from 1970; it was the first widely marketed SSRI. First approval/introduction: US FDA December 1987 (Eli Lilly and Company).

Selectively inhibits presynaptic serotonin (5-HT) reuptake, increasing synaptic serotonin and producing antidepressant, anti-obsessional and anti-bulimic effects. Receptor / target profile: Potent selective SERT inhibitor (Ki ~1 nM); modest 5-HT2C antagonism and sigma-1 agonism.

Summary: Well absorbed; Tmax 6–8 h. ~95% protein bound. Metabolised by CYP2D6 to active norfluoxetine. Half-life 4–6 days (norfluoxetine 4–16 days) – steady state takes weeks; potent CYP2D6 inhibitor.
Depression: 20 mg once daily in the morning; may increase after 3–4 weeks up to 60 mg/day
Long half-life – dose changes take weeks to reach steady state
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
Use lower or less frequent doses (e.g. alternate-day) in cirrhosis.
Usual max 40 mg/day; watch for hyponatraemia.
Approved for depression (≥8 y) and OCD (≥7 y); monitor for suicidality and growth.
Use only if benefit outweighs risk; possible cardiac malformation signal in first trimester and persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn with late exposure.
Excreted in breast milk; breastfeeding generally not recommended.
Use with MAO inhibitors (allow 5 weeks after stopping fluoxetine before starting an MAOI)
Long half-life – effects persist after stopping
CYP2D6 substrates – TCAs, antipsychotics, beta-blockers, tamoxifen (reduced efficacy)
With or without food; avoid alcohol.
Mood/suicidality; sodium in elderly; glucose in diabetics (hypoglycaemia during treatment, hyperglycaemia on withdrawal).
Nausea, vomiting, seizures, tachycardia, QT changes, serotonin syndrome. Supportive care; activated charcoal.
TADS (JAMA 2004) – fluoxetine plus CBT was most effective for adolescent depression.
Cipriani et al., Lancet 2018 – fluoxetine among the best-tolerated antidepressants.
Best taken in the morning (may cause insomnia)
Long-acting – effects and interactions persist for weeks after stopping
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
